rule: sofar-core owns exactly the hook shapes cli/fast.ts's SUBCOMMANDS list (six as of r1-fixes 4077c9a), `statusline` and the hidden `fold`; any further argv shape needs a Decision citing D15 and this one.
chose: D15's owned surface reads as "the hook shapes cli/fast.ts owns" rather than a fixed count: since r1-fixes 2.5 (self-improve 1.2) the shim routes SIX hooks — session-start, post-tool, post-tool-failure, user-prompt, stop, session-end — plus statusline and the hidden fold; cli.rs dispatches `event post-tool-failure` as owned now (handler arrives with 2.5) and HOTPATH §Entry points and dispatch lists it.
over: Keeping cli.rs at five hooks until 2.5 and letting `post-tool-failure` fall through to the TypeScript CLI as "not ours".
because: The dispatcher mirrors runFast's SUBCOMMANDS exactly (HOTPATH §Entry points and dispatch); a shape the shim owns but the binary hands back would make 3.1's boot-stub dispatch route a hook to a binary that refuses it. The count in D15's rule was a description of the surface at the time, not the law — the law is "what the shim owns, and nothing else"; this restates it so a future hook added on r1-fixes is a merge, not a Decision.
